_what: The EDGE-CASE REGISTER (S3): every class of reference the corpus actually holds, the terminal (state, reason) a hunt must end it in, and why. Every `ref` is a REAL row — a work, an admission, an acquisition attempt or a held-queue line that exists today — and each row cites where it came from in `source`. Driven by qc/instruments/litkb_edge_run.py (live, in the workstream the manifest names) and by the same driver's `--replay` (a worker database, every route stubbed, no network). Graded by `qc/instruments/litkb_acceptance.py edges`.

_columns.id: the row name; it is also the CSV's `row_id` and the `--only` selector
_columns.class: the edge class this row carries. One real carrier per class; where the corpus holds no carrier the row says so rather than inventing one
_columns.ref: the reference exactly as a caller would give it
_columns.ref_scheme: what the caller DECLARES it is; null means the scheme is inferred from the shape
_columns.source: where this row came from — a survey section, a report line, or the read-only SELECT that found it
_columns.expected: the (state, reason) pair `litkb.hunt.hunt` must answer. Absent on a held_for_ruling row: the expected state IS the ruling
_columns.adjudication: why that pair, from code file:line plus the attempts history. The auditor adds its own key beside the builder's
_columns.live: mode (execute | waits-on-migration | replay-only | not-a-hunt), why, and whether the live run may spend. `waits-on-migration` is never written here: a row that NEEDS a migration carries `needs_migration` and the mode is decided at freeze by measuring db_migration_tip
_columns.replay: seed + stubs for the deterministic re-run: `inputs` (hunt kwargs), `seed`, `registry`, `fetch`, `routes`, `extract`, and an optional `expected` that OVERRIDES the row's when the replay database cannot hold the live precondition
_columns.asserts: extra checks beyond the pair — in_main, admission_state, new_admissions, attempt_status
_columns.held_for_ruling: question + evidence, for a row whose expected state only Kam can settle

_replay_stub_kinds.registry: none (404 to everything, a TERMINAL miss) · status:<n> (one status to everything) · record (a Crossref record for this row's DOI, so admission lands in main) · title_gate (the frozen Crossref search body of qc/fixtures/litkb_title_gate_wrong_work.json)
_replay_stub_kinds.fetch: explode (any call fails the row) · pdf (200 + the bytes fixture) · html (200 + a sign-in page) · status:<n> (that status, no bytes)
_replay_stub_kinds.routes: none (acquisition must not be reached) · acquirer (a synthetic acquire() return built from `outcome` + `route_detail`) · real-oa-raises (the REAL acquire() ladder restricted to open access, with litkb.acquire.open_access.fetch_open_access raising)
_replay_stub_kinds.extract: off (extract=False) · stub (extract_and_ingest returns a fixed artifact pair; `tei`/`docling` pick the reason) · raise:<ExceptionClass>

rows.source: Reports/LITKB_FIRST_WORK_2026-09-21.md:87-89 — paper-search `search_unpaywall` returned EMPTY for every DOI, including known gold-OA controls; the S2 scout used OpenAlex `pdf_url` instead and said so in every drop-off. rows.rule: AN EMPTY REGISTRY ANSWER IS NOT A FINDING OF NON-OA. `search_unpaywall` returning nothing for a gold-OA DOI is a tool fault on the SCOUT side, recorded here so no later reader mistakes it for evidence that these works have no open-access copy.

adjudication.builder: NOT A HUNT ROW. The fault is in `paper-search-mcp`'s Unpaywall connector, which litkb neither calls nor owns: `litkb.acquire.open_access` reaches Unpaywall through its own client, and no hunt state can carry a scout-side tool fault. Recorded with `live.mode='not-a-hunt'` and EXCLUDED from `executed` so the register keeps the instance without pretending the hunt vocabulary covers it.

live.why: a scout-side tool fault, outside the hunt's vocabulary; excluded from executed and from replay
